To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chromomagnetic operator is a promising avenue to search for new physics at the high luminosity LHC, and that a search for $b \bar b h$ events with a $h \rightarrow \gamma \gamma$ final state is the optimal way to do this.
the chromomagnetic $d=6$ dipole operator for $b$ quarks has not been constrained to date, but can be probed with a $b$ tagged Higgs plus dijets search in the H->gamma gamma channel.

the chromomagnetic operator for the bottom can yield a rate-independent signal in boosted $b \overline{b} h $ events, which can be used to constrain this operator at the 14~TeV LHC to cutoff scales as high as $\Lambda \simeq 6~{\mathrm{TeV}}$ with 3 ab$^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chromomagnetic operator for the bottom.
the detection of a new physics signal in the Higgs sector, which is distinct in flavor structure, chirality, and Lorentz properties from other dimension six Higgs operators.
a new operator for the bottom-quark that has been largely overlooked in Higgs coupling measurements, and which can be probed at the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chromomagnetic $B$ operator can be probed in the $B \rightarrow B h$ decay channel at the LHC with a 14 TeV center of mass energy and a luminosity of 3 $\text ab$^{-1}$, but the sensitivity of the search is limited by our ability to tag $b$-jets.
a chromomagnetic operator with $\Lambda \sim$ 1 TeV is not excluded by LHC data, but is excluded by LHC searches if it has $\Lambda$ as large as 6 TeV.
the chromomagnetic operator is the only one of the dimension six operators which can give a large signal of boosted $b \overline b h$ events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chromomagnetic operator can have a large effect on Higgs production and decay, but is difficult to detect.
the LHC will be sensitive to chromomagnetic dipoles with $\Lambda$ as low as $\sim 1~\text{TeV}$, but that this sensitivity will be improved with a $b$ tagged $h + {\rm dijet}$ search.
the chromomagnetic $ b$ dipole operator is a good place to look for new physics in the Higgs sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the $b \bar b h$ final state can be an effective tool in probing new physics that enhances boosted Higgs production.
the $b \bar b$ pair is a promising portal to new physics.
searches for boosted Higgses can probe physics beyond the Standard Model that is otherwise difficult to access.
